from.place: Since the finite ring $\Lambda=P_n$ is annihilated by an integer, $F_{\Et}$ is a torsion abelian sheaf, so the classical input of the source note (Th. 1.1 of SGA 4 1/2 and [Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) applies to $f_{\Et}$: the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}$ are constructible and zero for $q>2e$.

title: Constructibility of etale compact-support candidates over a qcqs base
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $p$ proper and $f=pj$, and write $Rf_!^{(j,p)}K=Rp_*j_!K$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], where $j_!$ is applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $Rp_*$ is the derived direct image for $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] have constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal H^q(Rf_!^{(j,p)}K)$ is a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GL0, label theorem-constructible-shriek, bounded-below finite-ring specialization; section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification (compact-support candidate)

proof.text: A finite ring $\Lambda$ is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finite set of elements. The sequence $0,1,2\cdot1,\ldots$ repeats, so some positive $N$ kills $1_\Lambda$, and therefore every $\Lambda$-module, including all sections and cohomology sheaves considered here, is killed by $N$. Thus the torsion and Noetherian coefficient hypotheses of the cited Stacks inputs hold without assuming invertibility. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence], we may choose a convenient compactification whenever needed and return to the originally fixed one at the end. For every auxiliary separated finite-type map to a qcqs base used below, [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification with quasi-compact open immersion and proper second map; the later steps check these hypotheses before applying the compact-support inputs.

We record the passage from sheaves to bounded-below complexes for any fixed compactification $(j,p)$ of a map $h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], its proper ambient scheme is qcqs. Extension by zero is exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]; applying [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to cycles and boundaries gives $\mathcal H^s(j_!L)=j_!\mathcal H^s(L)$ and preserves any lower bound $a$. The module sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and $p_*$ is additive left exact by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to $p_*$ and a bounded-below representative of $j_!L$: its page is $E_2^{r,s}=R^rp_*j_!\mathcal H^s(L)=\mathcal H^r(Rh_!\mathcal H^s(L)[0])$, it vanishes unless $r\geq0,s\geq a$, and its abutment is $\mathcal H^{r+s}(Rh_!L)$ with a finite filtration. If $Rh_!$ sends every constructible sheaf to constructible cohomology, every $E_2$ is constructible. By [thm-constructible-serre], each outgoing differential has constructible kernel. The image of an incoming differential is the kernel of its cokernel and is therefore constructible as well. Since the square of the differential is zero, this image lies in the outgoing kernel; the cokernel of that inclusion is the next-page term $E_{r+1}^{r_0,s_0}$ and is constructible. Induction on the page keeps every term constructible; each relevant entry stabilizes at a finite page by the spectral-sequence theorem. For total degree $t$ only $a\leq s\leq t$ occurs. Induction over its finite filtration, using extension closure, proves constructibility of $\mathcal H^t(Rh_!L)$. The same theorem shows the output vanishes below $a$, so it remains bounded below. This is a conditional argument, not an invocation of the item being proved.

source.place: Tag 0GL0 final paragraph; Derived Categories Tag 015J, label lemma-two-ss-complex-functor

proof.text: For any affine base $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-affine-line-shriek-sheaf-constructible] gives the sheaf hypothesis of step 2 for $\mathbf A^1_B\to B$. All coefficient hypotheses were checked in step 1. Step 2 therefore proves the assertion for every bounded-below constructible complex on this affine line.

For affine $Y$, prove the assertion for $\mathbf A^n_Y\to Y$ by induction on $n$. For $n=0$ use the identity compactification: identity extension by zero and identity direct image are the identity, directly from [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. For $n>0$, polynomial coordinates in [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] identify the projection with $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf A^{n-1}_Y}\to\mathbf A^{n-1}_Y\to Y$. The intermediate scheme is affine. The first factor sends a bounded-below constructible complex to one of the same kind by step 3, and the second does so by induction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-qcqs-composition] to identify the composite candidate with the candidate for $\mathbf A^n_Y\to Y$. The factors are separated of finite presentation since polynomial rings have finite presentations and their affine diagonals are closed.

Now suppose $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], write $B=A[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$. This quotient presents $f$ as a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_Y$ followed by projection. The closed immersion is of finite presentation because its ideal is generated by the displayed finite list, and is quasi-finite because each fibre is either empty or a closed subscheme of a point. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quasifinite-shriek-constructible] to obtain constructible cohomology for $Ri_!K$. It is bounded below as follows: choose its identity open compactification, so it is $Ri_*K$; the functor $i_*$ is left exact and its module categories are Grothendieck abelian, hence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] preserves the lower bound. Step 4 applies to $Ri_!K$. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-qcqs-composition] identifies this output with $Rf_!K$.

source.place: Tag 0GL0 second paragraph: closed immersion in affine space; Tag 0GK3

proof.text: Keep $Y$ affine and let $X$ be arbitrary as in the statement. Cover $X$ by finitely many affine opens $U_1,\ldots,U_m$; this is possible because it is qc. Each restriction is locally of finite presentation: at points of an open, shrink the affine presentation neighbourhoods to principal opens contained in it, using $B_b=B[t]/(bt-1)$. Its source is qcqs, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes it of finite presentation. Restrictions remain separated: their diagonals are the base changes of the closed diagonal along the open subschemes of the relative product; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] preserves closed immersions under base change. Constructibility of the restricted cohomology sheaves follows from [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local], since an affine open of a restriction is still an affine open of $X$; restriction is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and commutes with cohomology by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. Induct on an upper bound $m$ for the number of affine opens in such a cover, including empty opens. The case $m=1$ is step 5. For $m>1$ put $U=U_1$, $V=U_2\cup\cdots\cup U_m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], $U\cap V$ is covered by the $m-1$ affine opens $U_1\cap U_i$. The induction hypothesis applies to $V$ and $U\cap V$, while step 5 applies to $U$. The triangle [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-relative-mayer-vietoris] and the long exact cohomology theorem [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] give, in every degree $t$, an exact sequence $A^t\to B^t\to\mathcal H^t(Rf_!K)\to A^{t+1}\to B^{t+1}$, with $A=R(f|_{U\cap V})_!K|_{U\cap V}$ and $B=R(f|_U)_!K|_U\oplus R(f|_V)_!K|_V$. The end terms are constructible; finite sums are constructible by extension closure. The middle term is an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(A^t\to B^t)$ by $\ker(A^{t+1}\to B^{t+1})$, so [thm-constructible-serre] proves it constructible. If $m=0$, $X$ is empty and the empty covering forces every sheaf and its derived image to be zero.

source.place: Tag 0GL0 first paragraph: source induction using Tag 0GKN

proof.text: Finally cover $Y$ by affine opens $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $X_W=X\times_YW$ is qcqs and $f_W$ is of finite presentation; it is separated because its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The restriction of $K$ to the open $X_W$ has constructible cohomology: every affine open of $X_W$ is an affine open of $X$, the affine-local criterion applies there, and exact inverse image commutes with cohomology. Apply step 6 to $f_W$. Apply [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] to the cartesian square with common scheme base $S=Y$, bottom map $W\to Y$ and top map $X_W\to X$. The map $f$ is separated of finite type, $W\to Y$ is arbitrary as permitted by that theorem, and the coefficients are finite. Thus its output equals $(Rf_!K)|_W$; [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] identify its degree-$t$ cohomology with $\mathcal H^t(Rf_!K)|_W$. All these restrictions are constructible. The affine-local equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local] now gives constructibility on the original qcqs $Y$. Step 1 identifies this result with the originally fixed candidate $Rp_*j_!K$.
